summary: Two pinned MLX Metal implementations expose the same source-level stabilized exponential summary: update a maximum reference, rebase the accumulated denominator whenever that reference changes, and merge parallel partials only after aligning them to a common maximum.
normalized_steps: Initialize a local maximum reference and exponential denominator according to the enclosing operator's seed policy.
For each admitted score or score chunk, select a new maximum reference covering the prior summary and new values.
Multiply the prior denominator by exp(old_max-new_max).
Add exponentials of the new scores relative to the new maximum.
Merge parallel summaries by selecting a common maximum, rebasing every partial denominator to it, and summing the aligned denominators.
Finalize with the merged maximum and denominator while leaving full-probability regeneration versus value-weighted payload normalization to the enclosing operator.
observed_variants: The softmax implementation updates by N_READS-sized chunks, pads its tail, carries a maximum-and-denominator summary but no weighted payload, and re-reads the input to materialize the normalized row.
The attention implementation admits scores through mask branches, optionally seeds a denominator-only sink, and rebases a value-weighted payload with the same factors before normalization.

The SIMDgroup and threadgroup merge choreography, storage choices, barriers, mask and sink behavior, tail policy, weighted-payload state, and output strategy remain implementation facts rather than candidate invariants.
